newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bosnia says needs troops past '98 pullout deadline.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia says needs troops past '98 pullout deadline.

text.p: Foreign troops will be needed in Bosnia beyond the 1998 deadline for their withdrawal, Bosnian co-chairman Boro Basic said on Wednesday.
"Do we need international troops after the deadline? The answer is yes," Basic said in reply to a question at a news conference in Kuala Lumpur.
Basic and the other chairman of Bosnia's council of ministers, Haris Siladjzic, wound up a three-day visit to Malaysia to promote investment in the war-ravaged Balkan nation.
"It would, in my mind, be a mistake to withdraw too early," Basic said. "There is much more at stake in Bosnia than just the future of Bosnia."
Basic and Siladjzic endorsed the efforts of U.S. special envoy to Bosnia, Richard Holbrooke.
Holbrooke, who brokered the Dayton peace accords that ended the former Yugoslav republic's conflict in 1995, visited Bosnia, Croatia and Serbia last week.
Officials reported some progress had been made on issues that had stalled the peace process aimed at reconciling Bosnia's Moslem, Croatian and Serbian communities.
"Now is the time for implementation of the Dayton accords, not for negotiations," Basic said.
"We've had the design, now we need the construction." He said it was appropriate for Holbrooke, the "architect of the accords", to help get them implemented.
